osc.title: Operating System Concepts
osc.authors: Abraham Silberschatz, Peter B. Galvin and Greg Gagne

mcho.title: Understanding Operating Systems
mcho.authors: Ann McIver McHoes and Ida M. Flynn

introduction-and-types-of-operating-syst.why: The four managers, their tasks and the types of OS, which the course book follows closely.

architecture-kernels-and-shells.why: System calls, user and kernel mode, and monolithic, layered, microkernel and hybrid structures.

process-management.why: Process states, the PCB, context switching and the levels of scheduling.

threads.why: The benefits of threads and the many-to-one, one-to-one and many-to-many models the course book uses.

cpu-scheduling.why: FCFS, SJN, SRT, round robin and priority scheduling with worked job tables like the past papers.
Scheduling criteria, multilevel queues and real-time scheduling.

memory-management.why: Single-user, fixed, dynamic and relocatable dynamic partitions, as in the course book.

unix-and-shell-programming.why: Unix design, redirection, pipes and filters.
